small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose3d is the dominant cost (the post kernel is light); tuning the post kernel further won't move fast_p much. If staying with this structure, try fusing the bias-add of conv_transpose with sum_weight at conv output time, and ensure x is in channels_last_3d to make the LayerNorm-over-C reduction contiguous.
- Note: norm_shape is (out_channels,) = LayerNorm over C, but the current kernel reduces over W. This is a correctness concern — verify; if tests pass it may be coincidental due to symmetric data. Reduction axis must be C.
- Add autotune configs varying BLOCK over the C dim (32/64/128) with num_warps 4/8, num_stages 2.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.ConvTranspose3d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computes input × weight outer product and scatter-adds into the output grid with stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1. This is where the 19ms is spent — the post-processing kernel is already cheap.
- Fix the LayerNorm axis: norm_shape=(C,) means normalize over the channel dim per (n, d, h, w). Use channels_last_3d layout so C is contiguous; one program per (n, d, h, w) block computes mean/var over C, applies gamma/beta, then participates in the 2×2×2 avg-pool and GELU epilogue.
- Fuse conv_transpose epilogue (bias + sum_weight) directly into the conv kernel's store, then the second kernel handles LayerNorm(C) + AvgPool3d(2) + GELU in one pass on a channels_last tensor. This removes one full read/write of the (N,C,D,H,W) intermediate.
